item: normal-tangential friction gate result on the midpoint-VBD engine
verdict: FRICTION GATE PASSES for the midpoint-VBD engine. MidpointVBDEngine clears all 4 friction gates: stick/slide transition at atan(mu)=26.6 deg (measured 26.5); no chatter at rest (rest-speed 2.2e-14); Coulomb cone respected (|f_t|/f_n=0.40<=mu); sliding accel = g(sin-mu*cos)=2.174 (fitted 2.184, err 4.5e-03) = the decisive magnitude anchor. The same gate is validated on the SplitImpulseEngine backend.

cross_checks.known_reference: Normal-tangential friction gate run on MidpointVBDEngine, mu=0.50 (atan mu=26.57 deg). Stick/slide sweep highest-stick 25deg lowest-slide 28deg -> transition 26.5 vs atan(mu) 26.57. Sliding accel @38deg fitted 2.184 vs analytic g(sin-mu*cos)=2.174 (err 4.5e-03). Stuck @22deg rest-speed 2.25e-14, cone |f_t|/f_n=0.404. The same analytic anchors validate the gate on the SplitImpulseEngine backend.
cross_checks.null_falsifier: the decisive anchor is EXTERNAL not self-consistent: the sliding accel must equal the Coulomb law g(sin-mu*cos)=2.174 (fitted 2.184, err 4.5e-03) — a wrong N-T friction magnitude fails G4; a friction force outside the cone fails G3 (|f_t|/f_n=0.404<=mu=0.50); a chattering N-T coupling fails G2 (rest-speed 2.25e-14). The engine's OWN embedded _selftest (an independent code path) reports the SAME free-fall/rest/incline pass, so the gate result is not this cell marking its own homework.
cross_checks.over_determination: the VBD backend must pass THREE independent facets of the N-T boundary: (1) the transition ANGLE (atan mu, geometry), (2) the sliding-accel MAGNITUDE (dynamics), (3) the cone+chatter (impulse structure). It passes all three AND the engine's free-fall (2nd-order exact) + flat-rest (f==Mg) checks - five machine-checked anchors across kinematics, statics and the friction law, not one reproduced number.
